decision: Remove SpO2 prediction from new formal evaluation and performance comparison; retain historical replication/pilot outputs

facts.claim: BIDMC provides one exported PPG/Pleth waveform at125Hz and monitor physiological numerics including SpO2 at1Hz; documentation does not provide wavelength-separated raw red/infrared optics or raw AC/DC calibration.
Standard pulse oximetry exploits different absorption at red and infrared wavelengths and the ratio of pulsatile-to-DC ratios, with device calibration.
An oxygen saturation accuracy study compares simultaneous pulse oximeter estimates with arterial blood co-oximetry, not only another monitor numeric.

inference: A single exported waveform may statistically correlate with monitor oxygen saturation through patient state, pulse morphology, acquisition processing or cohort composition. This does not establish identifiable optical oxygen-saturation measurement or transportability to a wrist sensor. The claim is not that every conceivable single-wavelength inference is mathematically impossible under additional assumptions.
dataset_diagnostic: See spo2_scope_audit.json: source numerics concentrated near normal values and few independent low-reading patients. Constant baseline does not use PPG. Not directly comparable to old windowed model results.
future_valid_scope: Only reconsider as a separate oxygen-related hypothesis with suitable multiwavelength raw signals, clearly defined calibrated references, sufficiently diverse low-saturation episodes, patient-independent testing and device transfer.
RR_note: The manual two-annotator mean inter-breath-rate and <=2 breaths/min agreement rule follows the dataset paper; our nonoverlapping 32s sampling differs from its overlapping-window protocol.
